Archimedes' spiral  r = θ

1/6 Gray circles are spaced π/2 apart, so every labelled dot lands exactly on one. Hover a black dot for its values; click it to light up its angle ray and matching radius circle. Key idea: the radius is the angle, so both entries of every ordered pair are the same number.

plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 8: Further Applications of Trigonometry
plan.contextChunk: This figure plots Archimedes' spiral on a single polar grid across one full turn. The grid is a set of concentric gray circles about the origin crossed by gray radial spokes, with horizontal and vertical axes numbered by integers from -7 to 7 in both directions and tipped with arrowheads. A solid dark navy curve starts at the origin and sweeps counterclockwise, its distance from the center growing steadily as it goes, so the trace forms one open loop that never crosses itself and finishes on the positive horizontal axis at about six units out. Six filled black dots mark sample points along the curve, each tagged with an ordered pair whose two entries are equal: (pi/4, pi/4) just above and right of the origin, (pi/2, pi/2) directly above it near height 1.6, (pi, pi) out to the left at about three units, (5pi/4, 5pi/4) down and to the left, (7pi/4, 7pi/4) down and to the right, and (2pi, 2pi) at the loop's end on the right. Because the radius listed in each pair matches the angle listed beside it, the marked dots let the reader confirm the relation r = theta point by point, and the even widening of the loop between successive crossings of a given direction is what a radius growing in direct proportion to the swept angle looks like.

Gray radial spokes every 45° (π/4) crossing the concentric circles
Horizontal axis with arrowheads at both ends, integer ticks labeled -7 … -1, 1 … 7
Vertical axis with arrowheads at both ends, integer ticks labeled -7 … -1, 1 … 7
Solid dark navy curve: Archimedes' spiral r = θ for θ from 0 to 2π, starting at the origin and ending on the positive x-axis near x ≈ 6.28
Filled black sample dot at (π/4, π/4) — just above and right of the origin
Filled black sample dot at (π/2, π/2) — directly above the origin, height ≈ 1.57
Filled black sample dot at (π, π) — on the negative x-axis, about 3.14 units left
Filled black sample dot at (5π/4, 5π/4) — lower left, about 3.9 units out
Filled black sample dot at (7π/4, 7π/4) — lower right, about 5.5 units out
Filled black sample dot at (2π, 2π) — on the positive x-axis, about 6.28 units out
Ordered-pair labels in stacked-fraction form beside each dot: (π/4, π/4), (π/2, π/2), (π, π), (5π/4, 5π/4), (7π/4, 7π/4), (2π, 2π)
Moving tracer point on the curve with its radius segment from the origin (interactive layer)

interactions.label: θ (radians)
interactions.teaches: As θ increases the tracer point moves counterclockwise and its distance from the origin increases by exactly the same amount — the radius readout always equals the angle readout, which is what r = θ means.

interactions.label: Sweep the radius and draw the spiral
interactions.teaches: The spiral is generated by two steady motions at once: the ray rotates at a constant rate while the point slides outward along that ray at a constant rate, so each successive turn would sit a fixed distance farther out.
interactions.sample_note: The rotating radius segment lengthens as it turns and leaves the navy curve behind it.

interactions.teaches: Clicking a labeled dot lights its angle ray and its matching radius circle together, showing why the two entries of each polar coordinate pair are the same number.

demo_steps.title: Start at the pole
demo_steps.narration: At θ = 0 the radius is also 0, so the curve begins exactly at the origin. The tracer sits on the pole with no radius segment yet.

demo_steps.title: A quarter turn out
demo_steps.narration: Drag θ to π/2. The tracer has rotated a quarter turn counterclockwise and stands about 1.57 units straight above the origin — the plotted dot labeled (π/2, π/2).

demo_steps.title: Half a turn — radius π
demo_steps.narration: At θ = π the point lies on the negative x-axis, about 3.14 units out. The label (π, π) reads angle first, radius second, and both are the same number.

demo_steps.title: Three quarters and beyond
demo_steps.narration: Past 5π/4 and 7π/4 the loop keeps widening at a steady rate; the gaps between successive gray circles crossed by the curve stay uniform.

demo_steps.title: One full turn closes the loop
demo_steps.narration: At θ = 2π the curve returns to the positive x-axis but now about 6.28 units out instead of at the origin — one full revolution has pushed the radius out by 2π.

demo_steps.title: Watch it drawn
demo_steps.narration: Play the animation and click any labeled dot: the rotating ray lengthens as it turns, and each highlighted ray plus its matching circle confirms r = θ at that point.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Every marked point has identical coordinates because the radius IS the angle — steady rotation paired with steady outward motion is exactly what makes an evenly widening spiral instead of a circle.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Square plot centered on the origin. Background: light-gray concentric circles at integer radii 1–7 and light-gray radial spokes every π/4. Black horizontal and vertical axes with arrowheads at all four ends, integer tick labels from -7 to 7 (labels sit just off the axis, tightly spaced near the origin as in the original). The spiral is a single thick dark navy (≈ #1F3F6E) curve from the origin sweeping counterclockwise through roughly (0.55, 0.55) at π/4, straight up at π/2, left at π ≈ 3.1, down-left at 5π/4, down-right at 7π/4, ending on the positive x-axis near 6.28 — it never crosses itself and its distance from center grows linearly. Six filled black dots with ordered-pair labels written as stacked fractions in parentheses, placed just outside the curve at each dot (upper-right for π/4 and π/2, upper-left for π, lower-left for 5π/4, lower-right for 7π/4, upper-right for 2π). Interactive layer: a bright accent color (e.g. orange) for the moving tracer dot, its radius segment from the origin, the highlighted angle ray, and the matching radius circle; a small corner readout showing θ and r as equal values in both radian-fraction and decimal form.

Notice that the r-values are just the decimal form of the angle measured in radians. We can see them on a graph in the figure.

Archimedes’ spiral

Graph of Archimedes' spiral r=theta over [0,2pi]. Starts at origin and spirals out in one loop counterclockwise. Points (pi/4, pi/4), (pi/2,pi/2), (pi,pi), (5pi/4, 5pi/4), (7pi/4, pi/4), and (2pi, 2pi) are marked.

discrepancies: Polar grid spacing differs: the source shows ~4 concentric gray circles spaced by π/2 (≈1.57, 3.14, 4.71, 6.28) so that the plotted points land on grid circles; the generated figure draws 7 circles at integer radii 1–7, making the grid denser and breaking the visual link between circles and the marked radii.

Label placement of '(7π/4, 7π/4)' and '(5π/4, 5π/4)' sits slightly farther from its dot than in the source (no leader alignment), and the (π/4, π/4) label crowds the inner loop of the spiral more than in the original.
Fraction labels render noticeably smaller relative to the plot than in the source, reducing the label hierarchy (numeric tick labels and ordered-pair labels are nearly the same visual weight).
trigger_reset() calls hidePopup(), which is not part of the documented scaffold API; if undefined, the 'Reset to original figure' button will throw and fail to restore the default state.
evaluation.notes: A close, clean reproduction of the Archimedean spiral polar plot with correct navy curve, black sample dots, arrowheaded axes and fraction ordered-pair labels, plus a rich and pedagogically apt set of interactions (θ slider, sweep animation, step player, clickable points); main weaknesses are the integer-radius polar grid instead of the source's π/2-spaced circles, somewhat small label type, and a possibly undefined hidePopup() call in the reset handler.
action_items: Change the concentric gray grid circles to π/2 spacing (≈1.57, 3.14, 4.71, 6.28) to match the source and to make each marked point land on a grid circle.
Guard or remove the hidePopup() call in trigger_reset() (e.g. `if (typeof hidePopup === 'function') hidePopup();`) so the reset button reliably restores the step-0 state.
Increase the ordered-pair label font size (or raise the fontSize cap) so the fraction labels read comfortably at inline size and clearly outrank the axis tick numbers in hierarchy.
Nudge the (π/4, π/4) and (7π/4, 7π/4) label anchors closer to their dots and away from the curve, matching the source's placement.
